messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: GPL and derivative works
parts:
I dug a bit deeper into the linking issue, and
it's yet another legal grey area:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNU_General_Public_License#Linking_and_derived_works

The FSF apparently says that if you dynamically link to
GPL code and are not GPL, you're violating the GPL.
And R packages definitely get dynamically linked to R!

I'd have thought the package Jiqiang mentioned is
violating the GPL by trying to ACM-license an R package.

Anyway, I think we're OK if we:

1. BSD-license Stan

2. GPL-license RStan

The GPL contains a clause allowing GPL-ed code to link both
BSD and GPL code (which is what RStan does) without forcing
the linked BSD code to become GPL-ed itself.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: GPL and derivative works
parts:
On Friday, July 6, 2012 4:13:48 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I dug a bit deeper into the linking issue, and
it's yet another legal grey area:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNU_General_Public_License#Linking_and_derived_works

The FSF apparently says that if you dynamically link to
GPL code and are not GPL, you're violating the GPL.
And R packages definitely get dynamically linked to R!

I think by "link" the FSF means in the computer sense of a linker, rather than merely some association. Many R packages do link their compiled code to R. But R packages that only distribute R code (such as mi) don't.

Anyway, I think we're OK if we:

1.  BSD-license Stan

2.  GPL-license RStan

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: GPL and derivative works
parts:
On Fri, Jul 6, 2012 at 4:27 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
On Friday, July 6, 2012 4:13:48 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I dug a bit deeper into the linking issue, and
it's yet another legal grey area:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNU_General_Public_License#Linking_and_derived_works

The FSF apparently says that if you dynamically link to
GPL code and are not GPL, you're violating the GPL.
And R packages definitely get dynamically linked to R!

I think by "link" the FSF means in the computer sense of a linker, rather than merely some association. Many R packages do link their compiled code to R. But R packages that only distribute R code (such as mi) don't.

Yes, I also think linking refers to actually using a static or dynamic linking like ld.  I suspect the R packages fall more under the domain of "plugins" which is something of a gray area, particularly if they call GPL licensed code of the main package.  That said, the Linux kernel allows non-GPL'd plugins.

Cheers,
Marcus
